responsibility: Implements the FT32 backend’s executable target hooks and helper routines that turn the static target description into GCC behavior for calling convention, addressing legality, section handling, and final assembly output. This file defines how FT32 returns values and passes arguments (including partial register/stack placement, by-reference decisions, varargs setup, and return-in-memory rules), validates pointer and address-space modes, decides legitimate FT32 memory addresses, enables or disables LRA, and marks ELF symbols/sections for data versus program-memory placement. It also provides the asm printers for FT32 operands and addresses plus target-specific formatting helpers used by ft32.md, making it the main C implementation of ABI, address-space, and emission logic for the FT32 port.
same_name_distinction: Unlike ft32.h’s static target macros, ft32.md’s declarative RTL instruction patterns, and ft32.opt’s option declarations, this is the executable backend implementation file: it defines the FT32 target hooks and helper code that enforce the ABI and address rules at compile time, print FT32 operands/addresses for assembly output, and apply section/address-space decisions driven by the definitions in the other same-stem files.
